title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linear Contextual Bandits with Arbitrary Adaptive Action Sets
abstract: arXiv:2609.15170v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study stochastic linear contextual bandits with arbitrary action menus that may depend on the fixed parameter and the interaction history. We establish matching upper and lower bounds, up to logarithmic factors. Let $d$ be the dimension, $K$ be the menu size, and $T$ the time horizon. For $2\le K\le d$, we prove an upper bound $\widetilde O(K^{1/4}\sqrt{dT})$. When $T\ge d^2$, we further prove a lower bound $\Omega(K^{1/4}\sqrt{dT})$. Thus, for $T\ge d^2$ and $2\le K\le d$, the upper and lower bounds match up to logarithmic factors, and the polynomial dependence on $K$ is optimal. Compared with the previous $\widetilde O(\sqrt{dKT})$ bound, our upper bound improves the dependence on $K$ by a factor of $K^{1/4}$.   For $K\ge d$, we prove an upper bound $\widetilde O_{d,T}\left(\sqrt{dT}\min\{\sqrt d,(d\log K)^{1/4}\}\right)$ and a lower bound $\Omega\left(\sqrt{dT}\min\left\{\sqrt d,\left(\frac{d\log K}{\log(2d)}\right)^{1/4}\right\}\r

translated_title: 具有任意自适应动作集的线性上下文老虎机的近乎极小极大最优遗憾
translated_abstract: 我们研究具有任意动作菜单的随机线性上下文老虎机，这些菜单可能依赖于固定参数和交互历史。我们在对数因子范围内建立了匹配的上下界。设 $d$ 为维度，$K$ 为菜单大小，$T$ 为时间范围。对于 $2\le K\le d$，我们证明了上界 $\widetilde O(K^{1/4}\sqrt{dT})$。当 $T\ge d^2$ 时，我们进一步证明了下界 $\Omega(K^{1/4}\sqrt{dT})$。因此，对于 $T\ge d^2$ 且 $2\le K\le d$，上下界在对数因子内匹配，且对 $K$ 的多项式依赖是最优的。与之前的 $\widetilde O(\sqrt{dKT})$ 界相比，我们的上界将对 $K$ 的依赖改进了 $K^{1/4}$ 倍。对于 $K\ge d$ 的情形，我们证明了上界 $\widetilde O_{d,T}\left(\sqrt{dT}\min\{\sqrt d,(d\log K)^{1/4}\}\right)$ 和下界 $\Omega\left(\sqrt{dT}\min\left\{\sqrt d,\left(\frac{d\log K}{\log(2d)}\right)^{1/4}\right\}\right)$。
tldr: 本文针对动作集可任意自适应变化的线性上下文老虎机建立了近乎极小极大最优的遗憾界，通过匹配的上下界证明了对动作集大小的最优多项式依赖，将已有的 $\widetilde O(\sqrt{dKT})$ 遗憾界中对 $K$ 的依赖改进为 $K^{1/4}$。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes nearly minimax-optimal regret bounds for linear contextual bandits with arbitrary adaptive action sets, proving matching upper and lower bounds that improve the dependence on the action set size from $K^{1/2}$ to $K^{1/4}$, thereby achieving the optimal polynomial dependence on $K$.
